triggers.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative reads 'cluster with 18:6 is rejected - the construction that binds 18:6-18:7 is named at that row instead.' 'that row' names a corpus artifact, not the text, and the campaign register law (Prov strategy S8: no positional row refs; cross-row references are verse-anchored) bars it. E-18 arm applied: the embedded claim is byte-TRUE - שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל opens 18:6 and בְרִ֑יב closes its second colon, while 18:7 opens פִּֽי כְ֭סִיל and closes with וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו, an exact chiastic reversal on the repeated noun כְ֭סִיל. A true claim phrased in workflow register scores low. The seam itself is sound: skeleton 18:4 (mym `mqym dbry py 'ys nhl nb` mqwr hkmh) and skeleton 18:5 (s't pny rs` l' twb lhtwt sdyq bmspt) share no word-bound token, and 18:5/18:6 share none either, so the single-verse span and the high band survive.

Purely cosmetic here: the underlying construction claim re-derives from bytes (שִׂפְתֵ֣י כְ֭סִיל ... בְרִ֑יב against פִּֽי כְ֭סִיל ... וּ֝שְׂפָתָ֗יו, on the repeated כְ֭סִיל), so no evidence is lost.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only (strongest_rejected_alternative): replace the clause with a text-register, verse-anchored formulation, e.g. 'cluster with 18:6 is rejected: 18:6 and 18:7 bind to each other by a lips/mouth chiasm on a repeated noun, leaving 18:5 outside.'

triggers.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative reads 'cluster with 18:18 is rejected - the pairing that binds 18:18-18:19 is named at that row instead.' 'that row' is an artifact reference barred by the Prov strategy S8 register purge. E-18 arm: the embedded claim is byte-TRUE at the lexeme level - 18:18 opens מִ֭דְיָנִים and 18:19 carries the qere וּ֝מִדְיָנִ֗ים (pmarks_Prov.json kq Prov.18.19 = 1 note), the same plural noun across the seam. The row's own seam claims also hold: skeleton 18:16 (mtn 'dm yrhyb lw wlpny gdlym ynhnw), skeleton 18:17 (sdyq hr'swn brybw yb' wb' r`hw whqrw) and skeleton 18:18 (mdynym ysbyt hgwrl wbyn `swmym ypryd) share no word-bound token in either direction, and the K/Q disclosure is inventory-correct (pmarks kq Prov.18.17 = 1; the unpointed inline ketiv יבא stands before the pointed qere וּבָֽא, the verb governing the second clause). A true claim in workflow register scores low.

Barred by the Prov strategy S8 register purge (no positional row refs; cross-row references verse-anchored). findings.proposed_change: Field repair only (strongest_rejected_alternative): re-cast in text register, e.g. 'cluster with 18:18 is rejected: 18:18 binds forward to 18:19 on the repeated disputes-noun, not back to 18:17.'

triggers.grounds: The medium_low label is honest in tone but masks a byte-false warrant, which is the lane's over-statement arm. device_notes fixes the load-bearing element itself: 'the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between 19:6 and 19:7, not on root-exclusivity.' That dependency is not in the bytes. 19:7 opens with כָּ֥ל, a quantifier and not a particle; the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י stands at token index 4 of 14, and the atnach (U+0591) sits on מִמֶּ֑נּוּ, so אַ֤ף כִּ֣י governs the move from 19:7a to 19:7b INSIDE the verse. Sweep of the skeleton phrase 'p ky: 6 verses book-wide (Prov.11.31, 15.11, 17.7, 19.7, 19.10, 21.27), token index 3-5 in every one - never verse-initial in Prov and never bridging a verse seam (Prov.19.10 shows the same intra-verse shape). With the a-fortiori warrant gone the cluster rests on a root-level tie only: 19:6 carries הָ֝רֵ֗עַ (word-bound skeleton hr`, 2 verses book-wide) and 19:7 carries מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ (word-bound mr`hw, 3 verses: Prov.12.26, 19.4, 19.7) - different forms, and the exact form mr`hw is shared with the NON-adjacent 19:4, which the row itself discloses. Under the C2 single_proverb default (strategy S1/S6) that residue does not carry a cluster at any band.

findings.claim: The cluster's designated load-bearing warrant - an a-fortiori dependency running from 19:6 into the opening of 19:7 - is byte-false; the a-fortiori operates inside 19:7.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative: 'the particle opening 19:7 grammatically depends on the claim just made in 19:6'; device_notes: 'the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between 19:6 and 19:7'. Bytes: 19:7's opening token is כָּ֥ל, a quantifier; the a-fortiori particle pair is אַ֤ף כִּ֣י at index 4 of 14 tokens, and the atnach sits on מִמֶּ֑נּוּ, placing that pair inside the verse's first half. Sweep: the skeleton phrase 'p ky occurs in 6 Prov verses and stands mid-verse (index 3-5) in all 6; Prov.19.10 carries the identical intra-verse a-fortiori shape. Residual cross-seam glue is root-level only (הָ֝רֵ֗עַ against מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ), and the exact form at 19:7 recurs at the non-adjacent 19:4, disclosed by the row.
findings.proposed_change: PROPOSAL (routes onward, not applied): retire the Prov.19.6-Prov.19.7 proverb_cluster and re-cut as two single_proverb rows, Prov.19.6-Prov.19.6 and Prov.19.7-Prov.19.7, per the C2 atomic default, disclosing the shared friend-root at 19:4/19:6/19:7 as texture in each. If the cluster is instead retained, the replacement warrant must pass the test that killed the original: no discourse-dependency claim across the 19:6|19:7 seam, root-level glue only, band dropped to low, with observed_substrate_signals, unit_type and strongest_rejected_alternative re-opened as dependent fields.

findings.claim: boundary_rationale places the spliced run at the opening of 19:7's second colon; the accents put it at the close of the first colon.
findings.grounds: Field text: '19:7 opens its second colon with מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ'. The spliced run's own final word מִמֶּ֑נּוּ carries the atnach (U+0591), so the run CLOSES the verse's first half; the second half opens with מְרַדֵּ֖ף. The row cites the very accent that disproves its position claim.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (boundary_rationale): 'the same root stands in 19:7 at מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ, closing the verse's first half at the atnach' - or drop the colon-position claim, which the row does not need.

findings.claim: device_notes uses cross-part workflow register ('the weaker of this part's clusters').
findings.grounds: device_notes: 'the weaker of this part's clusters, resting more on discourse-logic (dependency) than on an exact repeated lexeme.' 'this part' is a writer-part reference - process, not text - barred by the Prov strategy S8 register purge, which also bars part-range and file-order talk. The OW-1 retro scan carried the same evidence on this row under the REG lane (class cross_part_or_part_range) without promoting it to a trigger tag.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (device_notes): drop 'of this part' and state the weakness in text register, e.g. 'a cohesion tie weaker than an exact repeated lexeme.'

findings.claim: A verbatim WEB run is carried in straight quotes with no in-field web: ref.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative quotes "all the relatives of the poor shun him" in straight double quotes; WEB Prov.19.7 opens 'All the relatives of the poor shun him;' - verbatim apart from the initial capital. Prov strategy S8 and TOOLKIT.md require curly double quotes for WEB text PLUS an inline web: ref in the SAME field; the field carries neither. check_web_quotes.py cannot see it (it inspects curly-quoted runs only), which is why the row returned GREEN there.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (strongest_rejected_alternative): re-quote as a curly-quoted WEB run with an inline web:Prov.19.7 ref in the same field, or paraphrase without quotation marks.

triggers.grounds: The flagged sentence is 'sets up a contrast (quarrelsome wife/dripping vs. prudent wife/Yahweh's gift) that only works read as a pair'. The E-05 test requires naming a count OBJECT: there is none. The clause is a modal claim about the recoverability of an inter-verse contrast, not an occurrence, exclusivity or density claim, so no sweep digit is possible or owed; check_universals.py fires on the lexeme 'only' alone (its other five hits on this slice are 'first pleader' and three instances of 'first colon', plus a WEB quotation containing 'all'). The underlying cohesion would in any case survive a digit: word-bound skeleton 'sh occurs in 9 Prov verses (Prov.6.26, 6.32, 7.10, 11.22, 18.22, 19.13, 19.14, 30.20, 31.30) and 19:13-19:14 is the only adjacent pair among them; 19:13 closes מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה and 19:14 carries אִשָּׁ֥ה in its own second colon. No overclaim.

findings.claim: observed_substrate_signals asserts the repeated noun stands 'at the same line-final slot' in both verses; the bytes and the row's own rationale say the slots differ.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals[0] = 'exact repeated noun at the same line-final slot'. Bytes: 19:13 ends אִשָּֽׁה (verse-final, carrying the silluq/meteg U+05BD), but 19:14's אִשָּׁ֥ה is followed by מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת, which carries the verse-final silluq - so the noun is NOT line-final in 19:14. boundary_rationale states the correct, contrary fact ('colon-final, verse-final' at 19:13 against 'colon-medial' at 19:14), so the substrate signal contradicts its own driver field. The two attested forms also differ at byte AND accent_stripped tier (merkha against silluq); 'exact repeated noun' holds at skeleton tier only, and no tier is named.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (observed_substrate_signals): replace with 'the same wife-noun in both second cola, verse-final at 19:13 and colon-medial at 19:14 (skeleton tier)' - the positional contrast is the row's actual argument.

findings.claim: The 19:14 splice contains the very word the sentence says stands after it.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: '19:14's אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת "a prudent wife" instead sits colon-medial in the second colon ... and before the closing "prudent" adjective'. The spliced run is two words and already contains that closing adjective מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת; as a run it is verse-final, not colon-medial, so the sentence describes the splice as standing before part of itself. Splicing only אִשָּׁ֥ה cures it.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (boundary_rationale): splice only the noun for the position claim, and cite the full two-word phrase separately where the gloss 'a prudent wife' is wanted.

triggers.grounds: Calibration is sound; the band is neither over- nor under-stated. The strategy names 22:17-21 as an expected low-confidence region (S7: in-verse seam plus LXX-divergent text) and as the C3 prologue (S6), so span and unit_type admonition_unit follow the book's own reading; parent C3 Prov.22.17-Prov.24.22 matches S5 and the row straddles no collection seam. The seam warrant is tier-1 and in-verse as the book requires: 22:17 opens הַ֥ט אָזְנְךָ֗ plus וּ֭שְׁמַע, and דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים stands mid-verse at tokens 3-4 of 7, which the row states explicitly and argues 'from the clause itself and not from a title'. Tier-3 corroboration is inventory-correct and correctly typed: pmarks_Prov.json marks Prov.22.21 = PE, cited as petuchah/pe, single-witness, as corroboration and never as driver. The K/Q crux is real and correctly located: pmarks kq Prov.22.20 = 1, with the unpointed inline ketiv שלשום standing before the pointed qere שָׁלִישִׁ֑ים. The honest residue holding the band down is stated in device_notes - two governing movements inside the five verses (imperative address at 22:17-18 with its motive כִּֽי נָ֭עִים, then first-person disclosure at 22:19-21) plus the unresolved numeral crux - and frontier_flag_considered is true. No whole-chapter cap applies. The row's other defects are field-level and recorded separately.

findings.claim: The 23:1 corroboration is byte-false as written and is drawn from the wrong verse.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'Prov.23.1 ... opens an unrelated court-and-dining scenario sharing no skeleton token with 22:17-22:21, corroborating this unit's close at the 22:21 petuchah'. Bytes: 23:1 opens כִּֽי and 22:18 opens כִּֽי, repeating it at token index 2 - a skeleton token IS shared. The claim holds only for CONTENT tokens, the unit the book's texture metric actually uses. Separately the corroboration is inapposite: the verse standing at this unit's close is 22:22 (cited elsewhere in the same row), not 23:1, four verses past the seam.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (boundary_rationale): qualify to 'no shared content token' and argue the close against 22:22, keeping 23:1 in device_notes as following texture only.

findings.claim: The 22:19 gloss covers a word outside its splice.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'an infinitive clause, לִהְי֣וֹת בַּ֭יהוָה (oshb:Prov.22.19, "so that your trust may be in Yahweh")'. The splice is two words; the gloss's 'your trust' renders מִבְטַחֶ֑ךָ, which is not in the splice. Gloss extent must equal splice extent.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (boundary_rationale): extend the splice to לִהְי֣וֹת בַּ֭יהוָה מִבְטַחֶ֑ךָ, or cut the gloss back to the two spliced words.

triggers.grounds: A well-calibrated low-band row with sound grounds. The single-verse span is byte-warranted: 23:12 opens the imperative הָבִ֣יאָה לַמּוּסָ֣ר לִבֶּ֑ךָ with no motive clause (skeleton hby'h lmwsr lbk w'znk l'mry d`t carries no ky), while the left neighbour 23:11 closes a prohibition-plus-motive pair and shares no word-bound token with it (skeleton ky g'lm hzq hw' yryb 't rybm 'tk). unit_type admonition_unit for a one-verse governing imperative is the S6 clarifying amendment's ruled shape (B-8 precedent). The one live cross-seam device is disclosed on BOTH sides, satisfying the toolkit's cross-seam cohesion rule: this row names the לַמּוּסָ֣ר root recurring at 23:13 in מוּסָ֑ר and declines to fuse, and the 23:13-14 row discloses the same tie as texture - the neighbours argue the seam compatibly. The stated reason for the band is specific rather than boilerplate (a general, unaddressed call to attention against the named child-and-rod application), and frontier_flag_considered is true. The device_notes comparison is byte-true: 22:17 and 23:19 each open multi-verse addresses (הַ֥ט אָזְנְךָ֗ וּ֭שְׁמַע, שְׁמַע אַתָּ֣ה בְנִ֣י וַחֲכָ֑ם) and both verses are carried in boundary_evidence_refs, so check_refs_mirror is satisfied (GREEN across the slice). No disclosure object touches the span: pmarks_Prov.json holds no marks, paseq or kq entry at Prov.23.12 or at the front-seam verse Prov.23.11. Neither over- nor under-stated; no findings.

The band's stated reason does not bear on the boundary, and the boundary evidence is stronger than the band. device_notes: 'the K/Q density leaves the exact wording of verse 24 less certain than the boundary decision itself' - by its own words the WORDING is the uncertain object and the boundary decision the more certain one, so nothing stated supports holding the boundary confidence at medium_low. Meanwhile the cross-seam evidence is a two-root envelope the row never names: 23:24 carries the joy-root pair גִּ֣יל/יָ֭גִיל at its head and the qere יִשְׂמַח at its close, and 23:25 opens יִֽשְׂמַח and closes וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל - both roots cross the seam, in reversed order, not the single root the row cites. Tier truth on the one recurrence the row does name: יִשְׂמַח against יִֽשְׂמַח is NOT byte-equal and NOT accent_stripped-equal (23:25 carries meteg U+05BD, which accent_stripped retains); they match at skeleton tier only, and no tier is named. The K/Q digit itself is correct (pmarks_Prov.json kq Prov.23.24 = 4, matching the four inline pairs גול/גִּ֣יל, יגול/יָ֭גִיל, יולד/וְיוֹלֵ֥ד, וישמח/יִשְׂמַח). Confidence reads under-stated on a reason that is not about the boundary.

findings.claim: device_notes calls both cross-seam verbs third-person jussive wishes about the parents' joy; 23:24 is an indicative infinitive-absolute construction and the row's own rationale calls it a general maxim.
findings.grounds: device_notes: 'Both יָ֭גִיל (oshb:Prov.23.24, ketiv/qere, single-witness) and יִֽשְׂמַח (oshb:Prov.23.25) are third-person jussive wishes about the parents' own joy'. Bytes: 23:24 sets גִּ֣יל immediately before יָ֭גִיל - the intensifying infinitive-absolute-plus-yiqtol shape, matched by the parallel qere pairs וְיוֹלֵ֥ד and יִשְׂמַח in the same verse. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so both witnesses' renderings settle it: WEB Prov.23.24 renders indicatively while WEB Prov.23.25 renders jussively, and boundary_rationale itself calls 23:24 'the general maxim' against 23:25's 'applied wish', so device_notes contradicts its own driver field. The unit_type conclusion (no governing second-person imperative or vetitive, hence proverb_cluster rather than C3's operative admonition_unit) survives, which is why this is not scored high.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (device_notes): 'Verse 24 states an indicative maxim built on an infinitive-absolute intensification, verse 25 turns it into a third-person wish; neither carries a governing second-person imperative or vetitive, so the span stands outside C3's operative admonition_unit category.'

findings.claim: The medium_low band rests on a wording-certainty statement the row itself distinguishes from the boundary decision, while a second byte-visible cross-seam root goes unnamed.
findings.grounds: device_notes gives the K/Q density as the reason and in the same clause rates the wording 'less certain than the boundary decision itself'. Unnamed supporting bytes: besides the smh recurrence (יִשְׂמַח against יִֽשְׂמַח), the gyl root also crosses the seam - גִּ֣יל and יָ֭גִיל at the head of 23:24 against וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל at the close of 23:25 - giving a reversed two-root envelope rather than a single shared root. On the row's own evidence the boundary reads better than medium_low.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (device_notes plus confidence): name the second root and the reversed envelope, keep the K/Q density as a wording caveat only, and re-band the boundary decision upward - routed onward for adjudication, not applied.

triggers.grounds: The band is held on a corpus-wide generalization the book's own bytes refute, so the low label masks a defective warrant rather than recording honest uncertainty. device_notes: 'Confidence is held at medium_low because the three-verse reading rests on treating 24:23's heading-maxim as joined to its own illustration and resolution rather than as a free-standing header verse, the pattern the book's other headers follow elsewhere.' Bytes: the closest structural analogue, 10:1, does exactly what 24:23 does - the header clause מִשְׁלֵ֗י שְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה is followed IN THE SAME VERSE by a complete antithetic proverb בֵּ֣ן חָ֭כָם יְשַׂמַּח אָ֑ב וּבֵ֥ן כְּ֝סִ֗יל תּוּגַ֥ת אִמּֽוֹ; and the divrei-hakhamim seam at 22:17 stands mid-verse inside its own imperative clause (דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים, tokens 3-4 of 7). Only 1:1, 25:1, 30:1 and 31:1 are header-only verses, and none of them carries an independent maxim that could have been joined to anything. The seam is otherwise well-warranted: גַּם אֵ֥לֶּה is verse-initial (prov_device_inventory: gam-elleh verse-initial at 24:23 and 25:1), and pmarks_Prov.json marks Prov.24.22 = SAMEKH, correctly typed and single-witness-disclosed as corroboration rather than driver. An unnamed inclusio further supports the three-verse span - verse-final טֽוֹב at 24:23 against verse-final בִרְכַּת at 24:25, where verse-final twb occurs in only 12 of 915 Prov verses (2:9, 13:21, 14:14, 14:22, 15:23, 16:29, 19:8, 20:23, 22:1, 24:23, 24:25, 28:10), of which 24:23/24:25 is the only pair within five verses. Confidence reads under-stated on a false reason.

findings.claim: The stated reason for the medium_low band is an unanchored corpus-wide claim about the book's other headers that the bytes refute.
findings.grounds: device_notes asserts that a 'free-standing header verse' is 'the pattern the book's other headers follow elsewhere', with no verse anchors and no digit. Re-derived from the header spine (prov_device_inventory: mishle verse-initial at 1:1 and 10:1; gam-elleh at 24:23 and 25:1; divrei at 30:1 and 31:1; divrei-hakhamim at 1:6 and 22:17): 10:1 carries מִשְׁלֵ֗י שְׁלֹ֫מֹ֥ה followed by the complete proverb בֵּ֣ן חָ֭כָם יְשַׂמַּח אָ֑ב וּבֵ֥ן כְּ֝סִ֗יל תּוּגַ֥ת אִמּֽוֹ in the same verse - the identical header-plus-maxim shape the row treats as anomalous at 24:23 - and 22:17 carries דִּבְרֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֑ים mid-verse. The generalization is therefore false precisely where it is load-bearing, and it is stated in corpus register without verse anchors (E-18 arm).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (device_notes plus confidence): drop the generalization or replace it with the verse-anchored true fact that 10:1 carries the same header-plus-maxim shape, and re-band the boundary decision upward - routed onward for adjudication, not applied.

findings.claim: Two splices in boundary_rationale carry glosses that reach past the spliced words.
findings.grounds: (1) 'the heading's own maxim, הַֽכֵּר פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט (oshb:Prov.24.23, "to show partiality in judgment is not good")' - the negation 'is not good' renders בַּל טֽוֹב, outside the three-word splice. (2) 'verse 25's adversative, וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים (oshb:Prov.24.25, "but to those who convict, it will be pleasant")' - 'it will be pleasant' renders יִנְעָ֑ם, outside the one-word splice. Gloss extent must equal splice extent.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair (boundary_rationale): extend the splices to הַֽכֵּר פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט בַּל טֽוֹב and וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים יִנְעָ֑ם, or cut both glosses back to the spliced words.

findings.grounds: pmarks_Prov.json paseq records 1 seg at Prov.24.24, interior to the span Prov.24.23-Prov.24.25; no field of the row mentions it. The Prov toolkit lists paseq among the disclosure inventories and the standing rules extend symmetry completion to 'every other disclosure object', and the same writer wave disclosed a span-interior paseq elsewhere (M8-Prov-289 carries 'oshb:Prov.19.7 (paseq, single-witness)'), so the practice was live. Scored low and marked convention-level rather than validator-level: check_marks.py's symmetry arm covers PE/SAMEKH only, so the tool reports no gap here, and the inventory is count-only, so presence alone may be disclosed - never position.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: add 'oshb:Prov.24.24 (paseq, single-witness)' to boundary_evidence_refs with a presence-only mention and no intra-verse position claim.
